title: Entity resolution probabilístico
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S30.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts adjudicated USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S29 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED. Duplicate candidate pairs, mutable decisions, free-form evidence refs and stale entity state are not trustworthy training/evaluation truth.
required_carry_forward: canonical pair identity with A<B plus UNIQUE(A,B) or equivalent
immutable/versioned decision labels and exact evidence/source provenance
real pytest gates rather than print-only diagnostics

roadmap_expectation.T1: normalización/comparadores exact-edit-token-fecha; missingness informativa y frecuencia
roadmap_expectation.T2: blocking, candidate recall, combinaciones, costo y pares imposibles
roadmap_expectation.T3: pesos/probabilidad/umbrales; entrenamiento-estimación, clerical review y cluster consistency
roadmap_expectation.T4: labeled pairs, split por entidad, pairwise/cluster metrics y error slices
roadmap_expectation.gate: Testable Entity Resolution Engine con benchmark sintético etiquetado, blocking medido, comparadores explicables y cola de revisión; ER solo decide misma entidad

live_site.tagline: Motor de entity resolution testeable: benchmark etiquetado, blocking medido, comparadores explicables y cola de revisión

runtime_adversarial_checks.implication: missingness becomes perfect evidence in one comparator
blank-but-present text is treated as observed disagreement
same visible name can disagree by normalization form
comparators do not share one normalization contract
prose says omit missing but code cannot
absence of evidence becomes a negative identity decision
invalid numeric score is silently treated as uncertainty rather than rejected
zip silently discards missing prediction and yields false perfect metrics

runtime_adversarial_checks.observed: e1,e2,e3 one predicted cluster; gold only e1-e2; caller pred_pairs=[e1-e2] -> quality 1.0, while enumerating all co-cluster pairs -> 0.3333
blank name/city records collapse to key '|'
runtime_adversarial_checks.implication: missingness can create giant artificial blocks

external_research.use: blocking trade-off and multiple-rule union semantics
trained parameters and match weight log2(m/u)
probabilistic linkage requires model parameter estimation
thresholds selected/evaluated against labelled data and precision-recall trade-off
common-value agreements carry less evidence, but via explicit TF/model semantics
mailbox local-part case-sensitive by protocol; domain case-insensitive
example.com/example.org are reserved documentation domains; example.pe is not listed

findings.title: PREREQUISITE_TRUTH_STORE_NOT_CREDITABLE
findings.evidence: S30 says S29's pair/decision store feeds the engine, but S29 audit confirmed duplicate canonical pairs, mutable decisions, unconstrained labels and free-form evidence refs.
findings.attack: Training/evaluating from those rows can duplicate examples, mutate historical labels or detach evidence after the fact.
findings.defense: S30 uses synthetic examples and does not explicitly claim production data ingestion.
findings.impact: A probabilistic engine can learn/evaluate against non-reconstructable truth and then export clusters as if evidence were stable.
findings.fix: Validate canonical pair uniqueness, immutable/versioned labels, source/entity version and evidence provenance at the S29→S30 boundary.

findings.title: TESTABLE_ENGINE_WITHOUT_PYTEST_GATES
findings.locator: tagline/reference promotion + all 8 theory code blocks
findings.evidence: The section calls the engine testable and invokes S27/S28 suite, but theory blocks end in print outputs rather than pytest assertions/failure gates.
findings.attack: A behavior-changing regression can still exit 0 if printed output is not inspected.
findings.defense: The blocks are demonstrations, not the final You Do suite.
findings.impact: The section's defining gate remains observational rather than executable in the canonical lesson.
findings.fix: Turn comparator, blocking, threshold, cluster and evaluation contracts into collected pytest tests.

findings.title: SCORE_ROLE_CONTRADICTION
findings.evidence: Opening/job text says the score only orders a human queue, while T3-A performs auto_match/non_match and T3-B auto-unions pairs into clusters.
findings.attack: Learner cannot tell whether score is advisory-only or can trigger automatic identity merges/rejections.
findings.defense: The ethical intent is to distinguish identity decisions from fraud/risk conclusions.
findings.impact: Contradictory automation boundary undermines human-control semantics.
findings.fix: State explicitly that identity scores may drive bounded auto-match/non-match only when calibrated/validated; fraud/risk remains out of scope, and uncertain/insufficient evidence routes to review.

findings.title: UNRESERVED_SYNTHETIC_DOMAIN
findings.evidence: Fixtures repeatedly use @example.pe. IANA reserves example.com/example.org and special-use .test, not example.pe.
findings.attack: Copied fixtures can accidentally target a registrable/routable namespace.
findings.defense: No email is actually sent in theory.
findings.impact: Unsafe habit crosses into later integration workflows.
findings.fix: Use @equipo.test or @example.com.

findings.title: EMAIL_LOCAL_PART_CASE_COLLAPSE
findings.locator: T1-A comparators.py / I Do exact email
findings.evidence: exact() casefolds the entire email; RFC 5321 requires preserving/treating mailbox local-part case sensitivity while domain is case-insensitive, even though case-sensitive mailboxes are discouraged.
findings.attack: Two distinct mailbox local-parts can become an exact identity agreement.
findings.defense: Most modern providers behave case-insensitively and pedagogical fixtures are synthetic.
findings.impact: An exact comparator can manufacture strong identity evidence.
findings.fix: Preserve raw email; normalize domain case; make any provider-specific local-part canonicalization an explicit, tested policy rather than universal casefold.

findings.title: COMPARATORS_LACK_SHARED_UNICODE_NORMALIZATION
findings.evidence: exact/token use casefold+split, edit uses raw strings, blocking separately requires accent folding; NFC vs NFD José scores 0 in exact/token.
findings.attack: The same visible identity receives different evidence solely due to Unicode representation/comparator path.
findings.defense: T2 intentionally demonstrates accent-folding as a blocking lesson.
findings.impact: Comparator inconsistency corrupts weights and candidate recall.
findings.fix: Define one shared normalization pipeline with explicit field-specific policies and test NFC/NFD before all comparators/blocking.

findings.title: EDIT_EMPTY_EMPTY_BECOMES_PERFECT_MATCH
findings.evidence: edit_sim('', '') returns 1.0 while exact/token return missing and prose says two empties are not agreement.
findings.attack: A missing name can contribute maximal evidence if routed through edit comparator.
findings.defense: Mathematically edit distance of two empty strings is zero.
findings.impact: Mathematical similarity is incorrectly promoted to identity evidence in violation of the section's missing contract.
findings.fix: Apply missing precondition before edit/date comparators; return None/ComparisonResult(missing).

findings.title: DATE_COMPARATOR_MISSING_CRASH
findings.evidence: date_sim(None, valid_date) raises TypeError.
findings.attack: Real missing birth dates are expected by T1-B but date comparator cannot represent them.
findings.defense: T1-A says comparators assume observed inputs.
findings.impact: The public comparator API is brittle and the missing contract is not centralized/enforced.
findings.fix: Use a wrapper/result type that checks missing before every comparator and carries observed/missing state.

findings.title: WHITESPACE_IS_NOT_MISSING
findings.evidence: Only None or exact empty string is missing; whitespace-only values are treated as observed disagreement/agreement after casefold.
findings.attack: Source cleaning commonly yields whitespace placeholders.
findings.defense: Earlier normalization may be intended to trim fields.
findings.impact: Pipeline behavior depends on undocumented preprocessing order.
findings.fix: Normalize/strip first or define missing via canonicalized value and test whitespace-only inputs.

findings.title: FREQUENCY_TABLE_DOMAIN_UNVALIDATED
findings.evidence: freq 0 raises ZeroDivisionError; negative count returns negative identity weight.
findings.attack: Malformed or stale frequency tables create invalid scores.
findings.defense: The toy dictionary contains only positive counts.
findings.impact: The heuristic lacks a basic data contract.
findings.fix: Validate finite positive counts/support and define unseen-value policy.

findings.title: FREQUENCY_WEIGHT_NEVER_REACHES_SCORER
findings.evidence: frequency_weight is demonstrated separately; pair_score uses static weights and never consumes per-value frequency adjustment.
findings.attack: Outcome promises frequent-value downweighting but decision path ignores it.
findings.defense: It is presented as a didactic heuristic rather than full FS term-frequency adjustment.
findings.impact: A learned concept has no effect on the actual matching decision.
findings.fix: Carry effective per-field/per-value contribution into the scorer and explanation, or narrow the outcome to conceptual demonstration.

findings.title: INFORMATIVE_MISSINGNESS_ONLY_NARRATED
findings.evidence: Prose says model missingness by source_system; no code accepts source_system or estimates source-specific missing patterns.
findings.attack: MCAR warning has no executable consequence.
findings.defense: The section intentionally stays with a simple observed-field scorer.
findings.impact: Outcome overstates treatment of informative missingness.
findings.fix: Add source-aware missingness diagnostics/policy or explicitly defer modeling and narrow the claim.

findings.title: MISSING_BLOCK_KEYS_COLLIDE
findings.evidence: Missing/blank name and city map to the same key '|'.
findings.attack: Many incomplete records can create the exact monster block T2-B warns against, and may generate low-quality comparisons.
findings.defense: The fixture has complete name/city fields.
findings.impact: Missingness can explode candidate cost and contaminate candidate sets.
findings.fix: Fail/route missing blocking attributes or use multiple safe rules with explicit missing-key policy and max-block guard.

findings.title: BLOCK_KEY_NONE_CITY_CRASH
findings.evidence: rec.get('city','')[:3] crashes when city exists with None.
findings.attack: Schema missingness may be represented as null, not absent key.
findings.defense: Synthetic fixture uses strings.
findings.impact: Blocking fails before scorer on valid missing-data states.
findings.fix: Normalize null/blank explicitly and validate field type.

findings.title: CANDIDATE_RECALL_NO_POSITIVE_SUPPORT_CRASH
findings.evidence: len(gold & candidates)/len(gold) raises ZeroDivisionError when a slice contains no gold matches.
findings.attack: Evaluation by slice can legitimately have zero positives.
findings.defense: Main synthetic gold contains one match.
findings.impact: Metric code is not robust and can hide unsupported slices.
findings.fix: Return NA/None with support=0 and always report denominator.

findings.title: BLOCK_COST_FORMULA_NOT_DEDUPED_ACROSS_OR_RULES
findings.evidence: sum C(n_b,2) is exact for disjoint buckets from one partition, but multiple OR blocking rules can produce the same pair more than once before dedup; Splink reports cumulative unique comparisons across rule lists.
findings.attack: Learner may sum per-rule bucket costs and overstate actual unique scored pairs or miss rule-order effects.
findings.defense: The code accepts one list of disjoint block sizes, where the formula is valid.
findings.impact: Cost estimation does not generalize to the multi-rule strategy taught immediately before it.
findings.fix: State the scope and, for OR rules, compute/deduplicate candidate pair identities or use cumulative comparisons.

findings.title: MISSING_DENOMINATOR_CONTRADICTION
findings.evidence: Prose says missing fields are omitted from numerator and denominator; pair_score iterates all weights and TypeErrors when a similarity is None.
findings.attack: The central missingness policy is not implemented in canonical scorer.
findings.defense: The You Do starter later contains an observed-key variant.
findings.impact: Theory code contradicts the lesson's most important missing-data safeguard.
findings.fix: Build observed keys first and compute numerator/denominator only from finite non-None similarities.

findings.title: ZERO_EVIDENCE_AUTO_NON_MATCH
findings.evidence: No observed fields yields score 0.0, and decide(0.0) returns non_match.
findings.attack: Absence of evidence becomes evidence of different identity.
findings.defense: 0.0 is a convenient numeric fallback.
findings.impact: Directly violates missing≠disagreement and can create false negatives without human review.
findings.fix: Represent insufficient evidence separately (None/abstain) and route to review/no-decision, not non_match.

findings.title: THRESHOLD_CONTRACT_UNVALIDATED
findings.evidence: No validation for finite score or 0<=t_low<t_high<=1; t_high=.5,t_low=.9 makes score .7 auto_match.
findings.attack: Misconfiguration can invert/overlap policy regions silently; NaN falls through to review without being rejected.
findings.defense: Defaults are sensible in the toy fixture.
findings.impact: A configuration error can auto-merge records under nonsensical thresholds.
findings.fix: Validate score finite/in-range and threshold ordering before decisions.

findings.title: THRESHOLDS_AND_WEIGHTS_NOT_ESTIMATED
findings.evidence: Weights and .9/.5 thresholds are hardcoded; no training/selection function consumes the labelled training split or business cost/capacity.
findings.attack: Roadmap explicitly calls for entrenamiento/estimación and the prose says threshold choice has asymmetric consequences.
findings.defense: The section labels the scorer didactic and permits hand-set weights.
findings.impact: The main decision policy is asserted rather than evaluated.
findings.fix: Separate didactic baseline from an executable threshold-selection exercise on train labels; freeze selection before holdout evaluation.

findings.title: PROBABILISTIC_TITLE_WITH_NO_PROBABILISTIC_ESTIMATION
findings.evidence: No prior match probability, m/u estimation or conversion to match probability is executed; current Splink/Fellegi-Sunter materials define trained match weights from m/u and probabilistic scoring.
findings.attack: Weighted average similarity is not itself probabilistic ER.
findings.defense: The prose explicitly says simplified didactic and not calibrated probability.
findings.impact: Section title/roadmap competency is not achieved by canonical theory code even though the disclaimer prevents a worse misconception.
findings.fix: Either implement a minimal genuine FS estimation path or rename/narrow the executable claim to an interpretable heuristic ER baseline that prepares for probabilistic ER.

findings.title: CALIBRATION_TERM_OVERLOADED
findings.evidence: 'Calibración' is used for tuning weights/thresholds while the score is explicitly not probability-calibrated; later curriculum uses calibration in the reliability/Brier sense.
findings.attack: Learner may conflate threshold tuning with probability calibration.
findings.defense: The paragraph defines its local meaning.
findings.impact: Terminology creates future conceptual debt.
findings.fix: Call this 'ajuste/selección de pesos y umbrales'; reserve probability calibration for reliability calibration.

findings.title: CLERICAL_QUEUE_RECORD_INCOMPLETE
findings.evidence: Prose requires actor/timestamp/actions; code stores only pair, score and explain.
findings.attack: No reviewer identity, decision state, artifact/version, timestamps or evidence provenance exists.
findings.defense: The list is a minimal in-memory illustration.
findings.impact: Review cannot be audited or reconciled with S29 truth-store semantics.
findings.fix: Use a review item/decision contract with pair_id/version, source/evidence refs, allowed actions, actor, timestamp and status.

findings.title: COMMENT_AS_HUMAN_APPROVAL
findings.evidence: The code comments 'clerical: aprueba e3-e4' and directly calls uf.union without validating/storing an approval event.
findings.attack: A source-code comment substitutes for the human review that gates a destructive cluster merge.
findings.defense: The code is illustrating the effect after approval.
findings.impact: The learner sees no executable boundary between proposal and approved merge.
findings.fix: Pass an immutable approved decision record from S29 into merge logic and reject uncertain/missing/unapproved states.

findings.title: UNION_FIND_CANNOT_ENFORCE_NEGATIVE_CONSTRAINTS
findings.evidence: Prose says review contradictions such as A=B, B!=C, A=C; UnionFind stores only positive connectivity and no non_match constraints.
findings.attack: The advertised contradiction check is impossible with the shown data structure alone.
findings.defense: Union-Find is appropriate for transitive positive closure and prose warns about bridges.
findings.impact: A bridge can merge entities despite an explicit negative clerical label.
findings.fix: Maintain cannot-link/non-match constraints and validate proposed component merge against them before union.

findings.title: AUTO_UNIONS_HAVE_NO_SCORE_OR_PROVENANCE
findings.evidence: e1-e2 and e2-e3 are literal 'auto matches' unioned without score, threshold version, comparator contributions, source versions or decision ids.
findings.attack: Clusters exported to S31 cannot be reconstructed from evidence.
findings.defense: They are tiny synthetic setup edges.
findings.impact: The graph boundary inherits opaque identity merges.
findings.fix: Every union must consume a validated pair-decision artifact with provenance and decision policy version.

findings.title: LABEL_SPACE_PRINT_NOT_ENFORCEMENT
findings.evidence: The allowed labels are printed as a static list; no API validates incoming label values or blocks fraud/other strings.
findings.attack: S29 already allows arbitrary decision labels.
findings.defense: The ethics boundary is repeated in prose/callout.
findings.impact: A stated safety boundary has no executable gate.
findings.fix: Use enum/check constraint and explicit parser rejecting out-of-domain labels.

findings.title: EVALUATION_DISCONNECTED_FROM_ENGINE
findings.evidence: T4-B uses hardcoded y_true/y_pred, hardcoded clusters and pred_pairs unrelated to T2 candidates, T3 scores/thresholds or T4-A test split.
findings.attack: Metrics can remain unchanged while the engine logic is broken.
findings.defense: Toy vectors isolate metric formulas for teaching.
findings.impact: The promotion gate does not actually evaluate the engine it claims to close.
findings.fix: Generate holdout predictions from the frozen S30 pipeline and feed those exact pair ids/labels into pairwise and cluster metrics.

findings.title: PRF_ZIP_TRUNCATION_FALSE_PERFECT_METRICS
findings.evidence: prf([1,0],[1]) returns precision=recall=F1=1.0 because zip silently ignores the unmatched second label.
findings.attack: Missing predictions can disappear from denominators.
findings.defense: Canonical vectors have equal length.
findings.impact: Evaluation helper can produce a materially false green.
findings.fix: Assert equal nonzero lengths, aligned pair ids and allowed labels before metric calculation.

findings.title: METRIC_LABEL_DOMAIN_UNVALIDATED
findings.evidence: Only exact integer 0/1 comparisons count; unexpected labels/booleans/None can silently fall outside tp/fp/fn accounting.
findings.attack: S29 decision labels are currently unconstrained strings.
findings.defense: Synthetic vectors are binary integers.
findings.impact: Dirty label data can silently shrink effective support.
findings.fix: Validate schema/domain and report support/confusion counts.

findings.title: COCLUSTER_QUALITY_CAN_HIDE_TRANSITIVE_OVERMERGE
findings.evidence: Function divides over caller-provided pred_pairs instead of enumerating all unordered pairs that the predicted clusters co-locate. A 3-node predicted cluster with gold only e1-e2 scores 1.0 if caller passes only edge e1-e2, but true pair precision across the cluster is 1/3.
findings.attack: Union-Find's transitive closure creates implied pairs not present in the edge list.
findings.defense: The demo explicitly passes the only predicted pair in its tiny scenario and labels metric simplified.
findings.impact: Exactly the overmerge failure cluster metrics are meant to expose can be missed.
findings.fix: Derive all co-cluster unordered pairs from predicted clusters or use established cluster metrics; never trust a hand-supplied edge list as the cluster denominator.

findings.title: EMPTY_SUPPORT_REPORTED_AS_ZERO_PERFORMANCE
findings.evidence: Empty gold or empty predicted pair sets return 0.0 without support metadata.
findings.attack: No evidence is conflated with measured zero quality/completeness.
findings.defense: Returning 0 avoids division errors in toy code.
findings.impact: Small slices become misleading and incomparable.
findings.fix: Return NA/None plus numerator/denominator/support.

findings.title: ERROR_SLICES_OUTCOME_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
findings.evidence: Code prints only integer error indices; no source/missing_phone/common_last_name/city attributes are joined or aggregated into slices.
findings.attack: Outcome promises actionable error slices but no slice is calculated.
findings.defense: Paragraph calls the indices the seed of a slice.
findings.impact: The learner cannot diagnose systematic error from canonical evidence.
findings.fix: Carry pair metadata and aggregate FP/FN/support by declared slices on holdout predictions.

findings.title: PREVALENCE_REQUIRED_BUT_NOT_REPORTED
findings.evidence: Prose requires match rate/base rate in the gold; theory code reports only split counts/overlap.
findings.attack: P/R interpretation loses essential context in imbalanced ER.
findings.defense: The prevalence exercise appears later outside lessons-only theory.
findings.impact: Canonical theory does not demonstrate a metric it says must accompany evaluation.
findings.fix: Report positives/negatives/prevalence for train and holdout alongside P/R/F1.

findings.title: ER_FEATURES_AND_DECISIONS_DROP_S29_PROVENANCE
findings.locator: T1-A explain / T3-B queue / T4 labels
findings.evidence: Comparison outputs/explain dicts carry similarities only; pair/source/entity version, comparator/model version, label decision id and evidence refs are absent.
findings.attack: Later entity changes or stale replays can retroactively change what a training label appears to mean.
findings.defense: All data are synthetic and focused on algorithmic concepts.
findings.impact: S31 would receive clusters without reconstructable lineage to S29/source evidence.
findings.fix: Bind every comparison/prediction/label/union to canonical pair id, exact source/entity versions, normalization/comparator version, decision id and evidence ids.

rejected_or_bounded_false_positives.suspicion: Union-Find is intrinsically wrong for ER clustering
rejected_or_bounded_false_positives.reason: Connected-component closure is a legitimate clustering mechanism at a chosen edge threshold; the confirmed defect is failing to validate negative constraints/bridge merges and provenance.

rejected_or_bounded_false_positives.suspicion: A simple weighted scorer is pedagogically invalid
rejected_or_bounded_false_positives.reason: It is a valid interpretable baseline when honestly labeled. The finding is that it does not satisfy the section's probabilistic-estimation title/roadmap by itself.

rejected_or_bounded_false_positives.suspicion: Candidate recall 0.0 in T2-A is a bug
rejected_or_bounded_false_positives.reason: The lesson intentionally creates the failure to show accent-normalization impact; the real issues are missing-key policy, empty-gold handling and normalization consistency.
The canonical T4-A split correctly separates train, test and cross_split and reports zero entity overlap.

rejected_or_bounded_false_positives.suspicion: All empty-set metrics must mathematically equal zero
rejected_or_bounded_false_positives.reason: Different conventions exist; the pedagogical defect is returning 0.0 without declaring support/convention.
